subject: Biotechnology
title: Epigenetic Clocks
description: Learn Epigenetic Clocks in one minute.

hook.text: Your DNA methylation pattern reveals your biological age — some people are decades older inside than their birthday suggests.

buildup.text: Horvath's clock measures methylation at 353 CpG sites — predicting biological age within 3.6 years on average.

discovery.text: Accelerated epigenetic aging predicts earlier death, heart disease, and cancer — biology trumps chronology.

twist.text: Exercise, diet, and stress all shift the epigenetic clock — lifestyle interventions can slow biological aging.

climax.text: Clinical trials now use epigenetic age as an outcome measure — testing whether interventions truly slow aging.

punchline.text: Methylation marks count the years — epigenetic clocks reveal your true biological age.

quiz.question: What does an accelerated epigenetic clock indicate?
options: The patient's cells are dividing faster than normal
The patient's biological age exceeds their chronological age, predicting higher disease risk
The patient's DNA is mutating at an increased rate

details.summary: Epigenetic clocks measure biological age by analyzing DNA methylation patterns that change predictably with aging. They reveal that biological age can differ significantly from chronological age, predicting mortality, disease risk, and the effectiveness of anti-aging interventions.
details.whyItMatters: Biological age matters more than calendar age for health outcomes. Epigenetic clocks provide an objective measure of how quickly someone is aging, enabling evaluation of anti-aging interventions and early identification of accelerated aging before
takeaways: DNA methylation patterns change predictably with age across the genome
Biological age can differ by years from chronological age in individuals
Epigenetic age acceleration predicts earlier mortality and disease onset

faq.question: How accurately can epigenetic clocks predict biological age?
faq.answer: Horvath's multi-tissue clock predicts chronological age within about 3.6 years using 353 CpG methylation sites. More advanced clocks like GrimAge and DunedinPACE predict mortality and aging rate more accurately. Biological age differences of 5 or more years strongly predict health outcomes.

faq.question: Can you slow down your epigenetic clock?
faq.answer: Studies show exercise, healthy diet, and caloric restriction can slow epigenetic aging. Conversely, smoking, obesity, and chronic stress accelerate it. Some pharmaceutical interventions in clinical trials show epigenetic age reversal.
